title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of passenger cars and light vehicles (categories M1 and N1) with regard to braking (version 2.1.0)
scope_summary: Approves vehicle types with regard to their braking, covering the service, secondary and parking braking systems and related electronic, regenerative and electrical-transmission braking functions. It applies to vehicles of categories M1 and N1, excluding vehicles with a design speed not exceeding 25 km/h, vehicles fitted for invalid drivers, vehicles without manual braking controls for normal operation, and the approval of ESC and BAS.
scope_quote: 1.1 This Regulation applies to the braking of vehicles of categories M1 and N1. [...] This Regulation offers an alternative set of requirements for category N1 vehicles to those contained in Regulation No. 13. [...] 1.2 This Regulation does not cover: 1.2.1 Vehicles with a design speed not exceeding 25 km/h; 1.2.2 Vehicles fitted for invalid drivers; 1.2.3 The approval of the ESC and BAS systems of the vehicle. 1.2.4 Vehicles which are not equipped with manual braking controls intended for use during normal operation.

Does not cover approval of ESC and BAS systems (approved separately).

Vehicle categories M1 and N1 as defined in the Consolidated Resolution R.E.3 (ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.3).
Approval mark may be combined with marks of other Regulations under which the vehicle is approved (para. 4.5).

defined_terms.definition: Vehicles not differing in maximum mass, axle mass distribution, maximum design speed, type of braking equipment (incl. trailer braking or electric braking), engine type, gears, final drive ratios and tyre dimensions.
Combination of parts (control, transmission, brake proper) whose function is to reduce speed, halt, or keep a vehicle stationary.
The part actuated directly by the driver to furnish the transmission with the energy required for braking or controlling it.
Combination of components between the control and the brake linking them functionally, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, electric or mixed, including any energy reserve.
Components of the transmission which control the operation of the brakes, including the control function and necessary energy reserves.
Components which supply the brakes with the necessary energy, including the necessary energy reserves.
The part in which the forces opposing vehicle movement develop: friction brake, electrical brake, fluid brake or engine brake.
Equipment differing in component characteristics, materials, shape or size, or assembly of components.
One of the individual parts which, when assembled, constitutes the braking equipment.
Braking where the driver can increase or decrease braking force at any moment, force varies proportionally (monotonically) with control action and can be regulated precisely.
The maximum mass stated by the vehicle manufacturer to be technically permissible.

defined_terms.term: Hydraulic braking equipment with stored energy
defined_terms.definition: Braking equipment supplied with energy by pressurized hydraulic fluid stored in accumulators fed by pressure pumps with pressure limitation.
A braking system which, during deceleration, converts vehicle kinetic energy into electrical energy.
A device which modulates the action of the electric regenerative braking system.

defined_terms.term: Electric regenerative braking system of category A
defined_terms.definition: An electric regenerative braking system which is not part of the service braking system.

defined_terms.term: Electric regenerative braking system of category B
defined_terms.definition: An electric regenerative braking system which is part of the service braking system.
Instantaneous ratio of stored electric energy in an electrical storage device to its maximum storable energy.
An assembly of accumulators storing the energy used for powering the vehicle's traction motor(s).
Means whereby, with several braking sources on a common control, one source is given priority by phasing back the others.
Characteristic demonstrated at type approval relating the vehicle braking rate to the level of the braking input variable.
Function within a complex electronic control system actuating brakes to generate vehicle retardation, with or without driver action, from automatic evaluation of on-board information.
Function within a complex electronic control system automatically actuating individual brakes where retardation is secondary to vehicle behaviour modification.
Logic signal indicating brake activation as specified in paragraph 5.2.22.
Logic signal indicating emergency braking as specified in paragraph 5.2.23.
Vehicle hardware and software collectively capable of performing the entire Dynamic Driving Task on a sustained basis.
The real-time operational and tactical functions required to operate the vehicle.
Demand value for the braking force of a single electrically actuated wheel or axle.
A device that both generates and provides energy required for the braking system.
Device(s) capable of storing electrical charge and providing electrical power to the braking system transmission, counted as one per braking circuit supplied.
Device (e.g. battery, REESS, generator, fuel cell) supplying electrical power to the braking system's electrical storage device(s).
Electrical device(s) of an ETBS monitoring critical variables of electrical storage devices and deducing their capability to meet the Regulation's performance requirements.
Braking system where service braking force and transmission depend exclusively on driver-controlled use of energy from electrical storage devices.
Systems, functions or components supplied with energy from the same energy reserves as the braking system.

applicability_hints: This is a whole-vehicle approval: individual brake components (calipers, master cylinders, boosters, lines, ABS units, discs, drums, pads, pedals, parking brake actuators) are not approved separately but are covered as parts of the vehicle's braking equipment and listed in the application.
Brake discs and drums are tied to the vehicle approval via the identification code; changing them may require an extension of approval (section 7).
Brake linings may be assessed on an inertia dynamometer (Annex 7); replacement linings/discs/drums relate to UN R90 information in Annex 1.
Electric/hybrid powertrains fall under it via electric regenerative braking (category A or B), regenerative braking controls and traction battery state-of-charge test conditions.

Brake-by-wire systems are covered as Electrical Transmission Braking Systems including electrical storage devices, electrical supply (battery, REESS, generator, fuel cell) and energy management systems.

Any electronic function that actuates the brakes automatically (ACC, AEB, ADS, traction control, stability interventions) brings that electronic control system under Annex 8 as automatically commanded or selective braking, although ESC and BAS approval itself is excluded.
Stop-lamp activation logic and emergency braking (hazard flash) signal generation are governed by the braking signal and emergency braking signal requirements (5.2.22/5.2.23).
Auxiliary equipment sharing energy reserves with the braking system (e.g. hydraulic or electrical consumers) is subject to the braking energy requirements.
Changes in tyre dimensions, engine type, gear ratios, maximum mass or axle load distribution define a new vehicle type for braking.
For N1 vehicles a manufacturer may choose UN R13 instead of R13H; vehicles fitted with trailer braking equipment are within scope.
